what_this_is_en: Every substance named on every line of the enriched markdown, read independently of the extraction and asked only that: not roles, not quantities, not whether it matters. `specific` names one substance you could identify - a compound, a named mineral, an ISO common name, a development code that stands for one molecule. `generic` refers to a substance without naming one, and is counted apart because a solvent is sometimes an anaphor and sometimes the finding; the class terms this patent formulates with - lower alcohols, ketones, clays, nonionic and anionic emulsifiers, silicates - are here as generic, because they are how the patent names those ingredients. Spans are English because the engine checks them against the English rendering of the line, so a German line and the `> EN:` line paired with it are two keys over one English text and both carry the same spans. Table rows are lines like any other and are read as such; tables 1 to 7 hold band maxima, bond lengths and cell dimensions and name no substance except tembotrione in four captions. Excluded on purpose: plant genera and species, crop names, gene designations, trade names, instrument and software names, space group symbols, publication numbers, and the atom labels of the crystallographic tables, which are atoms inside one molecule rather than compounds; also formulation FORMS (suspension concentrate, wettable powder, granules), which are dosage forms and not ingredients, and role words whose substance is named in the same breath (the active ingredient, the active compound). A role word standing for a substance the document never names IS recorded, as generic, even where the article is definite: 'the solvent' of the process is not an anaphor back to anything, because nothing in this patent says what it is. Two deliberate departures from CN111440099B, the worked format: (1) line 61, the drawn structure, carries its SMILES as a specific mention, where the CN read filed no SMILES at all - the molecule really is on that line, it is tembotrione, and a SMILES joins by structure rather than by string; (2) the bare class words herbicides, safeners, fungicides, insecticides, acaricides and nematicides are recorded here as generic, where CN excluded 'herbicide' as a market descriptor, because in this document they are not descriptors of the extracted compound but stand-ins for the unnamed mixing partners of paragraphs [0044] to [0047]. In the two long lists the span is the base name and not the salt or ester variant the patent parenthesises after it, on the principle that made '20% aqueous methanol' span methanol: Acifluorfen (-sodium) is filed as Acifluorfen. Two spellings are preserved exactly as printed and are not corrected here: 'lodosulfuron', which is Iodosulfuron set with a lower-case L, and 'Pelargonsaure' (printed with an a-umlaut), which the translation left in German. 'Flumetsulam' is printed twice in the same sentence and is one mention. IMPORTANT, and it is a limit of this whole step: this is one language model reading a page another language model read. Where this list and the extraction agree, that agreement is weaker evidence than it looks, and nothing here can see a substance both of us missed. The line numbers in this file were REMAPPED after it was first written. The read was done against a 1169-line enriched document; 91 whitespace-only lines were then removed from 13 vision files and the document was rebuilt to 1078 lines, the same 1030 non-blank lines in the same order, and every key here was moved through the resulting old-to-new map and then re-checked against the rebuilt text rather than trusted. That rebuild happened because of this read: english_by_line() in resolve_translations.py aborted on this document at old line 98, since a vision paragraph whose zh holds a blank line before a table is written to the enriched file with that blank line while the walk's own body list drops blank lines, so the two desynchronised and Source() could not be built at all. It is worth recording that a completeness read is what turned that up: this step exists to find what the extraction lost in the half that fails silently, and it found a blocking defect in the half that is supposed to fail loudly, which is not what it is for and can evidently happen again.
verified_en: Every span below is a literal substring of the ENGLISH rendering of the line it is filed under, which is the text verify.py compares it with: `source.text_en.get(n) or source.lines.get(n)`. That text comes from verify.py's own Source class rather than a reimplementation, so the check and the engine read one definition of what line n says in English. After the blank-line fix Source constructs cleanly on this document with no patching: 1078 lines, 125 paragraphs, 118 aligned line for line and 7 unaligned. Spans were extracted from that text rather than typed: the systematic name, tembotrione and sulcotrione were found by scanning every line, and the 245 herbicide and 23 safener names were split out of the two long list lines by a parser, not transcribed. All 949 spans were then re-checked, one by one, against the REBUILT document at their remapped line numbers, and all 949 pass. Every substance-bearing paragraph is in the aligned set, so no span here rests on the unaligned rule that gives a source line the whole paragraph's English; the 7 unaligned paragraphs are front-page bibliographic blocks and the continuation of Tabelle 3, and they name no substance. Blank lines carry no key; every other line does, including the ones with nothing on them, because 'a reader looked here and found nothing' and 'nobody looked here' must not be the same colour.
